input.value: JsonSchema spy where getTypeValidator() is stubbed to return a non‑null mock TypeValidator

cases.description: When the schema has a TypeValidator (getTypeValidator() returns a non‑null instance), hasTypeValidator() should return true, exercising the true branch of the conditional.

input.value: JsonSchema spy where getTypeValidator() is stubbed to return null

cases.description: When the schema does not have a TypeValidator (getTypeValidator() returns null), hasTypeValidator() should return false, exercising the false branch of the conditional.

input.value: JsonSchema instance created via JsonSchemaFactory.fromJsonNode with schema node {"type":"string"}

cases.description: A schema that explicitly defines a single type should provide a non‑null TypeValidator, therefore hasTypeValidator() must return true.

input.value: JsonSchema instance created via JsonSchemaFactory.fromJsonNode with an empty schema node {}

cases.description: An empty schema contains no "type" keyword, so getTypeValidator() returns null and hasTypeValidator() must return false.

input.value: JsonSchema instance created via JsonSchemaFactory.fromJsonNode with schema node {"type":["string","null"]}

cases.description: When the schema defines a type array, the implementation creates a composite TypeValidator; hasTypeValidator() should therefore return true.

input.value: JsonSchema instance created via JsonSchemaFactory.fromJsonNode with schema node {"maxLength":5}

cases.description: Presence of other validation keywords (e.g., maxLength) does not create a TypeValidator; hasTypeValidator() must still return false.

input.value: JsonSchema instance created via JsonSchemaFactory.fromJsonNode with schema node {"type":123}

cases.description: The "type" keyword must be a string or an array of strings. Providing a numeric value causes the internal TypeValidator construction to throw a JsonSchemaException, which propagates out of hasTypeValidator().

input.value: JsonSchema instance created via JsonSchemaFactory.fromJsonNode with schema node {"type":[]}

cases.description: An empty array for the "type" keyword is not a valid definition. The validator creation fails and throws a JsonSchemaException, which should be observed when hasTypeValidator() is invoked.
Calling hasTypeValidator() on a null JsonSchema reference should raise a NullPointerException, as the instance method cannot be invoked on a null object.
